_comment: 1.12.2 line against legacy Just Enough Items 4.16.x, launched through the checkout's own Gradle run task (gradle launch) and through the harness's own run task (1.12.0/gradle/jech-uitest.gradle, task runClientTests): env.uitest selects the scenarios, so the client drives them itself and writes report.json, its captures and junit.xml into <game dir>/uitest before quitting, which is why the row declares no ready_when and no world -- jt's ready_when is a stopping rule for a client that would otherwise run forever, and the level the assertions are made against is the harness's own throwaway superflat creative world. Both artifacts ride the classpath rather than being staged into mods/: JECh because the harness run registers the checkout's sourceSets.main as the mod, and the JEI-line mod because a 1.12.2 JEI jar's access transformer is written in SRG member names, which never match the MCP-named members a dev client has -- measured on the jt-driven row, where jt's own staging of the raw jar ended the run in JEI's init with `IllegalAccessError: tried to access method net.minecraft.client.renderer.texture.TextureMap.initMissingImage()V from class mezz.jei.gui.textures.JeiTextureMap`. The checkout stages that jar itself, with the rules remapped (gradle/jech-uitest.gradle, stageUiTestDevMod), and -PdevMod=jei in env.gradle.args is what picks which JEI-line mod it stages. This row was declared `skip` from 2026-10-14 until the same day's revival: the 1.12.2 client could not be dev-run on this arm64 machine at all (LWJGL 2's macOS natives are i386/x86_64-only while every JDK here is arm64, and the instance launcher whose arm64 natives substitution used to carry the row was retired), and once the checkout's conditional arm64 natives repository made the client boot, two further blockers stood in the dev run -- JECh's own coremod NPE on getSource() and that same access-transformer mismatch. The narrative and the earlier measurements are in envs/README.md, 'The 1.12.2 rows and the gradle launch'. No 'Registering JEI pinyin search index' check here: that line is emitted by JechJeiPlugin.registerAdvancedSearch, and legacy JEI 4.16.1.301 has no mezz/jei/api/IAdvancedSearchRegistry to implement (75 classes under mezz/jei/api, none of them the search API; HEI 4.34.0 has it). With legacy JEI the integration is the classic ASM path instead -- its two markers below are the assertion, and the extra check pins the suffix-tree patch only this path applies.
